name: Western Algerian Berber
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Laoust, E. 1912. Etude sur le dialecte berbere du Chenoua compare avec ceux des Beni-Menacer et des Beni-Salah. Paris: Leroux.

sources.citation: Destaing, Edmond. 1907. Etude sur le dialecte berbère des Beni-Snous. Tome I. (Publications de l'École des Lettres d'Alger, Bulletin de correspondance africaine XXXIV.) Paris: Ernest Leroux. [Tome II, 1911]
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage 2245.60
sources.note: Marks accent diacritically on every transcribed word (p. 2 vowel table: 'â, ô, ê long et accentué; ā, ō, ē long et non accentué; á, ó, é bref et accentué; ă... très bref') and says (p. 2 n. 2) that isolated nouns were accented as if pronounced phrase-finally as direct objects; p. 192 notes that when gemination changes between sg. and pl. 'l'accent est alors modifié' (áḫḫām / iḫámměn). No rule of accent placement is stated; his marked forms show accent variously initial, penultimate, antepenultimate (árgāz ~ írgāzěn, afûnas ~ ifûnāsěn, iḍáṛṛěn).

sources.citation: Basset, René. 1895. Etude sur la Zenatia de l'Ouarsenis et du Maghreb central. (Publications de l'École des Lettres d'Alger XV.) Paris: Ernest Leroux.
sources.note: Nothing. 'Chapitre premier. Phonétique' is a table of consonant correspondences among Achacha, Haraoua, Ouarsenis, B. Halima, B. Menacer and Zouaoua; no accent remarks.

sources.citation: Chikhi, Hakim; Meharzi, Mohand. 2021. 'اللهجة الشنوية [The Chenoui dialect]', Afaq Ilmia (آفاق علمية) 13(4): 511-529. (in Arabic)
sources.note: Section 4.1 'al-sawtiyyat' covers initial-vowel loss and spirantisation tables only; no mention of stress (نبر).

sources.citation: Djemaï, Salem. 2019. 'Salah (Aït –/ Beni –) : un parler berbère menacé de l'Atlas blidéen', Encyclopédie berbère 42: 7157-7161. doi:10.4000/14u16
sources.note: Section 'Phonétique-phonologie': three vowels a i u without length + non-phonemic schwa, generalized spirantisation, treatments of /g/; nothing on accent.
